title: fix(github): reduce publication options delays
body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub publication options can spend their five-second request budget on PR display metadata that recovery does not use. The publication projection already returns state-only candidates, but the shared branch loader first fetched diff statistics and check rollups for up to three open PRs. Repeated recovery reads also fetched the same immutable commit/tree coverage proof again.

## User Impact

Opening GitHub publication options can reconcile previous publication attempts without waiting for unrelated PR statistics or checks. Current permissions, stale display fallback, and visible retryable failures remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing branch-cache owner now publishes list facts first and lazily shares optional metadata enrichment among display readers. Publication reads neither start nor await that enrichment. The display cap, all publication candidates, quota backoff, stale display fallback, and current-access checks remain owned by the same code. Pending metadata sharing now matches the prepared state/head signature, and replacement entries prevent a late older response from overwriting newer metadata.

Successful coverage proofs use the existing bounded retained-cache primitive (100 entries), keyed by credential scope, repository API root, PR head, accepted tree and source commit, with 90-second freshness. Each read still checks live authority and current PR candidates. Failures and pending credentialed requests are not cached. Existing visible, retryable options timeouts remain unchanged.

Runtime production LOC: **+58** across the three production modules; the standalone benchmark adds 206 developer-tool lines (**+264 non-test/non-doc lines total**). The growth retains the existing display/quota contract while separating its optional work, plus the bounded immutable-proof cache; there is no parallel publication loader or weaker authorization path. The benchmark is a separate developer tool with usage in its header.

## Evidence

Baseline: `5ed4aa230f8996b7747f654c5bf26ad2e2a8860a`. Synthetic owner benchmark: 40 branches with distinct heads, three open PRs with 100 checks plus a fourth merged PR, 65 concurrent readers, 2,048 cold session-list identities selected from a 10,000-identity space. No live GitHub, Team service, or production state was accessed. After the review repairs, two AB/BA timing pairs and two separate AB/BA sampled-allocation pairs:

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Process CPU/read, timing mean | 1,121 µs | 459 µs | −59.1% |
| Main-thread CPU/read, timing mean | 896 µs | 376 µs | −58.0% |
| Sampled allocation/read | 591,481 B | 126,499 B | −78.6% |
| Mean owner p95, 2,048 samples/arm/pair | 79.2 ms | 9.5 ms | −88.0% |
| Observed GC time/2,048 reads, untraced | 131.3 ms | 21.4 ms | −83.7% |
| Post-GC retained heap, timing mean | 200.4 MiB | 183.6 MiB | −16.8 MiB |
| RSS, timing mean | 777.7 MiB | 843.7 MiB | +8.5% |

Per 2,048 reads, list calls stay at 2,048; optional detail calls fall 6,144→0, check calls 6,144→0, and commit-proof calls 2,048→65 (concurrent cold requests retain separate live authority).

The separate slow-dependency case delays optional details/checks by 1.2 seconds: **p95 1,350.3→17.9 ms**, 260 samples per arm. Timing p95 was 103.4/55.0 ms on base and 7.9/11.1 ms on candidate. One-minute host load for the timing arms: base 36.5/46.1; candidate 44.9/44.5. Allocation arms: base 49.2/78.5; candidate 52.5/55.8. Slow-dependency arms: 81.7/84.8.

RSS rose 2.2% and 15.6% in the final timing pairs (+66.1 MiB mean). The preceding five timing pairs were +0.1% on RSS. Those earlier pairs also showed −71.2% main-thread CPU and −78.8% allocation. Retained heap consistently fell about 17 MiB. RSS is variable here, so this PR claims a CPU/allocation and retained-heap improvement, not an RSS improvement. No A/A rejection claim is made.

These are owner-path measurements, not end-to-end options, server-handler or whole-Gateway p95. The measurements target eliminated optional display work; no whole-Gateway load campaign was run. The final pending-metadata identity repair changes display-only work; the measured publication path is unchanged. Cold branch discovery and authoritative list reads can still require GitHub; this PR does not claim every options call is network-free.

### Validation

- Current-main regressions fail for the intended reasons: publication starts optional details; identical coverage reads fetch twice.
- Candidate: 39 tests across PR publication, ordinary PR reads and staleness; 21 coverage tests, including changed head/snapshot/credentials, expiry and revoked authority.
- All 30 focused options/RPC tests pass, including bounded timeouts, stale account reads and revoked authority (90 focused tests total).
- Changed-file formatting/lint, `git diff --check`, the export-name collision guard, and both closure guard files (38 tests) pass.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean at P0–P2. Regressions cover queued forced refreshes, warm/cold metadata failures, the 30-second retry window, and late old-head completion after a newer display result. The GitHub review finding is addressed and its thread resolved.
- Final head `3249fa122c0c0bada2bb042d910303100caff953`: [full CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41074052317) and [combined security gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41076321697). An earlier security-status publication hit GitHub HTTP 500 errors; the normal validation of the repaired head succeeded, without requesting a rerun.
- No test budget or baseline was raised. Broader proof belongs to PR CI; no manual Testbox lease was used.
